notes:
Play manual for Crumb Chase

Controls (exact console output when the control takes effect):
- Arrow Up: prints "TURN UP" and sets the mouse direction upward (KEYDOWN). Implemented in game/crumb_chase.py -> CrumbChaseGame.handle_events.
- Arrow Down: prints "TURN DOWN". Implemented in game/crumb_chase.py.
- Arrow Left: prints "TURN LEFT". Implemented in game/crumb_chase.py.
- Arrow Right: prints "TURN RIGHT". Implemented in game/crumb_chase.py.
- R key: prints "RESTART" and resets the maze, mouse, cats, crumbs, score and lives to initial state (3 lives, score 0). Implemented in game/crumb_chase.py.reset_game.
- Escape or window close: prints "QUIT" and exits. Implemented in game/crumb_chase.py.handle_events.

Gameplay observable console lines for scoring and end states:
- Each time a crumb is eaten the game prints: "[EVENT] SCORE:<current_score>" (flush=True). Implemented in game/crumb_chase.py.eat_crumb_at and game/entities.Crumb.eat.
- When all crumbs are eaten the game prints "WIN" and shows on-screen message "WIN - Final Score: <score>"; game movement freezes. Implemented in game/crumb_chase.py.
- When Lives reaches 0 the game prints "GAME OVER" and shows on-screen message "GAME OVER - Final Score: <score>"; game movement freezes. Implemented in game/crumb_chase.py.

Requirements -> implementing files (summary):
- Window title: game/crumb_chase.py sets pygame.display.set_caption('Crumb Chase').
- 15x15 grid maze: game/maze.py generates a 15x15 maze; drawing in game/crumb_chase.py draws the grid.
- Mouse (green), Cats, Crumbs: classes in game/entities.py; CrumbChaseGame constructs and renders them in game/crumb_chase.py.
- Movement rules (mouse moves tile-by-tile until a wall; cats move one tile at a time and at junctions pick a direction toward the mouse): implemented across game/entities.py (Mouse.update, Cat.update, Cat.choose_next) and orchestrated in game/crumb_chase.py.update.
- Score, Lives, Win/Lose, Restart, Quit, HUD: game/crumb_chase.py.

Runtime notes and limitations:
- The maze is procedurally generated and randomized on each reset. Start positions for mouse and cats are chosen as the nearest open tiles to preferred positions (center and corners).
- Cat routing uses a greedy Manhattan-distance heuristic at junctions (not global pathfinding). This implements the Plan's milestone 2 requirement as a local heuristic.
- Visuals use only plain coloured shapes (no images or sounds) per Plan.
- Movement speeds are tile-based: Mouse speed is 6 tiles/sec, Cat speed is 3 tiles/sec (tunable in game/entities.py / game/crumb_chase.py).

Exact commands the validator should send and expected console outputs to assert correctness:
1) Start game: window title should be "Crumb Chase".
2) Press Arrow key (e.g. RIGHT): expect console line "TURN RIGHT".
3) Move until stepping on crumb(s): expect repeated lines like "[EVENT] SCORE:10", "[EVENT] SCORE:20" etc.
4) Eat final crumb: expect "WIN" and on-screen text "WIN - Final Score: <score>".
5) Lose all lives by allowing cats to catch mouse: expect "GAME OVER" and on-screen text "GAME OVER - Final Score: <score>".
6) Press R after win or game over: expect "RESTART" and game reset to Score: 0, Lives: 3 and all crumbs present.
7) Press ESC or close window: expect "QUIT" and application exit.

Files implementing core logic:
- game/crumb_chase.py: main loop, input handling, HUD, rendering, orchestration of rules and state transitions.
- game/maze.py: Maze class, generation, is_open/neighbors/all_open_tiles.
- game/entities.py: Mouse, Cat, Crumb classes and movement/eating logic.

This play_manual was created fresh for the current build per the harness requirement. If you want sample deterministic input traces to reliably force a WIN or GAME OVER in an automated test, I can add a deterministic seed and fixed maze/start positions for a follow-up run; currently the maze is randomized each run.
